It's understandable that in any alpha there will be problems...but with Kingdoms there is no game full stop. Nothing works and there is little help/guidance in game. It crashes a lot, and it's full of bugs such as floating animals or villagers walking on water. The quests don't seem to work properly and the skill tree is nuts, and the menus are all badly aligned and all over the place. Unfortunately, the game promises a lot in the form of a sandbox 'do what you want experience' but delivers very little at present other than a flashy trailer which doesn't reflect the actual gameplay. Other reviewers are correct about it being a basic Unity engine game with no real AI or development beyond a few placeable basics and limited interaction.
Compared to Stranded Deep which was somewhat playable and enjoyable (although basic) on its alpha release, Kingdoms doesn't appear to have the fundamentals down yet to make it past an hour or so of confusing, clunky gameplay.
However, despite the negatives, there is a boat load of potential for Kingdoms to become a great game. Unfortunately, given the unpolished and sloppily released alpha it will be difficult to restore that yearning to see and test the improvements and follow the latest news and updates that I have with other games in the genre. This is one that I'll check back on in a year. Who knows, I might be suprised!

I really wanted to like this game, as the concept and plans of the devs are very exciting. Not only that, but they have been very active and helpful while also being very open to new ideas proposed by the players. The "plan" for this game seems to be to make into a M&B type RPG with a more open-world focused on surviving and crafting. Honestly, it's an AWESOME concept.
Unfortunately, it's just that. A concept. As it is, this game is riddled with gamebreaking bugs. Not to mention the moderate bugs that just annoy you. The combat is clunky and at the moment, downright horrible (though they claim they intend to make it much more interactive). Even on "fantastic" graphics settings, the models (NPCs, animals, etc.) in this game are ugly to look at, and there's not much variance in the climate/environment. The content right now is non-existent, and you'll maybe have 10-20 minutes of playtime before you get bored of glitchy bears, immortal citizens who walk by the bears unharmed, badly translated dialogue(Yes I understand it's a foreign game) and confusing leveling systems.
I can't in good conscience recommend this game. It is on all accounts an unplayable game. Just like every other early access game, it's something that promises a lot, but fails to deliver on every account. What I can say is this: If the devs keep their work up, follow the road map, and continue to iron out the clunky/unpolished aspects of it, this game may be worth buying in 6-7 months time.
Late February edit: This game has seen little to no progression and I stand by this review completely, and my review's complaints still stand. This game is still a don't buy.
May edit: Still little to no progression with the same content. Honestly I expected much more at this point. Still a no buy, still not anywhere near feeling complete. Each update on the roadmap has been delayed, and by this point they were supposed to be MUCH further then they've gotten. Spend your money elsewhere, honestly.

I wanted to like this game, but the experience was extremely frustrating.
First, the good:
1. The cash shop is no big deal. Mostly cosmetic and convenience items. The EXP bonuses for cash are small, only 30%. They don't create an immense divide based on shelling out loads of cash. Leveling doesn't take terribly long. The onyl thing worrying is the item that allows you to instantly revive where you died.
2. There's a large variety of classes, so you can play how you want to play. If you can't find a group, you can easily solo.
3. Cutesy anime art-style, if you like that kind of thing.
4. Getting round the map is convenient with warp scrolls and warp points, so you won't spend all day running all over the place.
Now .. the bad.
1. This game takes the primary purpose of an MMO -- having lots of other people to play with, and basically flushes it down the toilet. It takes far too long to be able to find and join a guild. Unless you're level 100, you are wasting your time even trying to find one, because of the pointless requirements to create one -- only ONE character class is allowed to create guilds, and that character has to be level 224. Why would you ever do that? It boggles the mind. Guilds are limited to 20 players initially, and can be expanded to a max of 35, further worsening those artificial restrictions. It will take you about 50-75 hours of play time to reach level 100 on your first character, BTW. So you basically won't have a guild to join until you've played the game for at least 50 hours.
2. All social aspects of this game are grossly lacking. Finding people to play with in the game is a pointless exercise in frustration. There's no system to look for groups except when queueing for a dungeon, and you have to stand still at the dungeon entrance while waiting in the queue. There is no region chat or way to create custom chat channels for people to join, like an LFG channel. The only way you can reach a large audience is by purchasing a 'megaphone' for real cash and sending a server-wide message that scrolls across the top of everyone's screen with it. A large chunk of players in the maps I was doing quests on were bots, anyway. All emphasis on being social and playing with other people is void. There is none of it. This is a solo-MMO game. Why would you play an MMO if you want to solo everything?
3. Buffs, buffs, buffs. This is another MMO that requires you to constantly manage copious amounts of short term buffs in order to be effective. You have to spam your buffs on yourself every 30-60 seconds, and you need to frequently return to town to get buffs from player character vendors to be able to beat enemies in a reasonable time frame.
4. The battle is rather simplistic, with really long cooldowns on your good abilities that you need to use to defeat monsters in a reasonable time frame. I was playing as a Hoplite, and I had to run around, gathering big groups and smash them with a skill on a nearly 30 second cool down. It made combat feel very slow.
6. Melee classes, once again, in yet another MMO, are mediocre at best. This is a constant issue in MMOs, and almost every new MMO that comes out suffers from this problem at launch.
7. Gold spammers. Bots. They've had an embargo on players for creating a new account for almost a MONTH and there's still tons of bots and gold spammers. Cripes.
So, overall, lotsof potential - but it falls extremely flat on its face due to truly confounding choices by the developers. I REALLY wanted to like this game, but the issues are just too glaring for me to stick it out any longer.

But, in all seriousness, this is a very mental-heavy game, and is a puzzle like no other.
Anyone who says this game isn't challenging, is only thinking of the combat, which can be rather easy, if you're prepared.
This game is very challenging in the puzzler sense, having you test your mental abilities and space-management skills.
I have played this game over and over again (despite what steam shows, I bought this game in way early access, and have only recently downloaded it on steam) and I can tell you, this game has replayability.
People should not dislike this game for an unstable Multiplayer, because Factorio is a SINGLEPLAYER game.
The idea that they would add Multiplayer at all wasn't until recently and I think its a cool idea, because you usually don't have muliplayer in these kind of games.
Now, I know this game isn't perfect, and I wish they would change or add some things in the future (which they will, this game is still early access and the developers have added a lot over the time its been in early access) such as-
- Harder to defend bases
When the aliens attack your base, it can be annoying, but if you have turrets in the right places, you never have to worry about it. In fact, the aliens are so predictable the usually only attack your walls at a specific point everytime. I think they should add more aliens that come along in the base raids and make things a little more complicated.
- Better trains
Now the train system in this game is really cool, but usually the only reason I use trains is because I think they'd look cool. The truth is, most games you can do just fine without them, because they can easily be replaced with long-distance conveyer belts, which provide a steadier, more reliant flow.
- More with Water
currently the only thing lakes and ponds do is allow you get water from them (using an offshore pump), and restrict your movement. I think you should be able to build boats and/or bridges to help this. This whole game is about conquering your nature as MAN and I think you should be able to conquer water too. Perhaps to balance to balance this, you could add aliens that swim, or attack only in water.
- More with combat
Like I said before, this a puzzler and space-management game, and isn't heavy on combat, but if they added more diversity in the combat system, it could provide whole new strategies to the game. There could be different types of turrets (Grenade turrets, Flamethrower turrets, etc.), new traps, such as electric fences or barbed wire, and new types of enemies to boot.
All in all, this is great game, and reccomend everyone to buy it, even though its in early access, because even if the developers suddenly stop working on it, this game is worth every penny.

This game, especially for a free to play, really impressed me, it succesfully combined features of arcade zombie games ( horde-survival modes, objective modes, different zombie types ... ) with extremly realistic dynamics ( such as bleeding, getting infected, having to manage your inventory and your stamina ) in a mix that can entertain both the casual and the hardcore zombie survival player.
However, the game is not without flaws, Il'l put a list of what I think is good and what I think it's bad about this game:
Good:
-Extremly well done official levels, especially for a free to play.
-Good realism concepts, having to take care of your health ( you can get infected and turn! ), your stamina, your inventory.
-Different difficulties make you able to switch from casual-mode to hardcore-survival however you like.
-A lot of mods for this game, especially new maps.
-Good first-person animations, there's an animation for practically every action you do ( healing yourself, reloading, checking how much ammo you have ).
-Decent graphics.
-Fun to play for the first times.
-The same levels can contain different weapons, different objectives and different zombie spawns, making each game-session in the same level feel a bit different.
Bad:
-Few official levels, half of wich being '' survival-mode '', wich feels the same every time.
-Bad third-person animations, often you can't understand what your teammate is doing with the object in his hands.
-Hitboxes and ragdoll collisions could use some improvements, it's really frustrating to get hit from something that shouldn't have hit you in a game where 1 hit can infect you and basically doom you to death.
-Maybe it's just me, however we just couldn't get the private servers up and running, forcing us to join public ones ( often modded with infinite ammo or full of people that wasted items and such ).
-Gameplay is somewhat methodical and repetitive, after the first hours, it kinda got boring for me.
Overall, for a free to play, this is a game I 100% recommend to try out, especially if you don't mind some of the flaws I found ( or if it was just me seeing them! ).

I was soft banned for altering my soul memory so I could co-op with my friends. Now I can only play singleplayer or with other softbanned players. Besides my mistake this is a great game. The people who created this world really know how to tie it all together perfectly. You'll pass through areas you've been before but with new purpose most times. You don't need a map because every inch of the world will have been explored and remembered. Not many games I've played can add purpose-per-square-step of map like that and I appreciate it.
The bosses are challenging and I feel like I actually learn things about the game, weapons and spells after vanquishing them. I'm a big fan of co-op and don't tend to enjoy pvp in any game but after having fought the various bosses you start to feel like you can face anything. I recommend getting as far as you can by yourself and pushing yourself further before even considering summoning a friend. You'll gain more if you can accomplish this yourself. If you don't, those lessons will just be pounded into you through PvP instead. You can't escape the nuances this game has to teach you about persistence and grit.
Don't be like me, don't even think about touching this game with a memory editor! Luckily the game is still 100% enjoyable singleplayer as it is in multiplayer.

I haven't put that much time into DS2 on PC but I've put over 200 hrs on XBOX360 and another 50 into SOTFS On PS4.
First of all: Dark Souls 2, and Dark souls 2: SOTFS are very good games.
The world is vast and engaging, and the story is vague but fascinating (albeit simple) even though it's the same basic story of its predecessor.
There is two main aspects of the game: PVE, and PVP.
The PVE is good by industry standard, but it may feel somewhat lacking to people who already played DS1. I personally liked it just as much.
The PVP has many balancing issues, as there is a lot of overpowered weapons and meta techniques, but it is also very fun and competitive when you know counter techniques for said metas.
The biggest issue with DS2 is the soul memory system, and I really wish fromsoft stuck with soul lever matchmaking.
Overall, I really enjoyed it and I will still be playing SOTFS on PS4 until the release of Dark Souls 3.

When Dark Souls II first was released, I had nothing but praise for the game. It looked gorgeous, ran well, and was well designed.
However, as a dedicated PvPer, I have always been a little turned off by how the game went about implementing PvP. To me, it was just never quite as good as the first Dark Souls was. Laggy netcode, poorly balanced weaponry, and a meta of max level due to the asinine Soul Memory system really have just dissuaded me from every playing this again.
In addition, the main criticsm I have of Dark Souls II is that From Software did not fully understand what made Dark Souls so special in the first place. Dark Souls was not a hard game, it was incredibly fair to you yet punishing if you continuously make mistakes. Dark Souls II is a hard game, but not for the right reasons. The majority of the "difficulty" came from throwing a horde of enemies at you at once. Bosses were not well designed and either brutally difficult or laughably easy. The only boss fight which I really loved in this was Sir Alonne because he was one of the few bosses that had a very well designed moveset.
I'd like to point out that I think that Dark Souls II is an 'alright' game, but it pales in comparison to its predecessor, Dark Souls.

Day 1: Hmm... Factorio? What idiot would buy this crap? I'll give it a shot.
Day 2: I've been playing for hours now. How on earth can this game be so fun? 12:00AM Already? Dang... maybe I should stop.
Day 3: I have bitten my fingers to the quicks. It keeps calling out to me I don't think I can help myself much longer. I should play. I HAVE TO PLAY.
Day 4: WHY ARE THE F****ING ALIENS SO ANNOYING? MY FACTORY IS IN SHREDS. I will have my revenge.
Day 5: My girlfriend came to me today. She says I should stop playing. She doesn't understand, no one understands.
Day 6: My girlfriend told me to make a choice, her or Factorio. Why would she do such a thing? Can't I love both? She gave me a day to decide. I only needed seconds.
Day 7: She looks longingly into my eyes, waiting for my final answer. I tell her I'm sorry. I simply cannot live without finishing my work. It has consumed me. I hurl myself into Factorio's strong arms, our bodies join in a Holy embrace between man and machine, it caresses my hair with it's machine-like hands, it tells me that I'm special. Oh Factorio, I will never leave you.
Day 8: The Aliens have come back again... I fixed that problem.
It's started to rain. I look up into the sky, thousands of corpses lay at my feet, I've done it, my factory is now autonomous, it no longer needs me. I wipe the remainder of purple blood from my gun as I walk towards my factory, the making of my own hands. I have done it.
The End:
The moon shines through my window, glistening on the metallic skin of the creature I have come to love so much.
"Did you like it?" it asks.
"I loved it, but now what?" I respond.
Factorio stands and extends its hand towards me, how many times have I felt those hands guide my own?
"It has only just begun, my child. Come with me, I have more to show you."
I reach out my hand, but it is no longer my own. I look into a mirror before taking that final step over the edge, I expected to see myself, but I did not. Instead, looking back at me through lifeless eyes, I saw a metallic creature. The Human Factory, everything I have ever created has led up to this, I have become a factory.

Why am I dreaming about conveyor belts? Why do I disdain eating cereal because I can't automate the process? Why does my wife accuse me of loving a video game more than my 11 month old son? Why is my posture starting to remind me of a large biter? Why am I worried that my Dodge Stratus can't withstand ramming into a large worm coming out of the ground? Why does my butt smell like poop? Why have I suddenly become pro-global warming? Why do I want to keep building and expanding walls all over my property? What the f*** is a constant combinator? Why did I research concrete so early? Why did I build 10,000 flame thrower ammo canisters before confirming how flame turrets worked? Why do my friends look at me funny when I tell them I have to finish my spaceship? Why do I get an erection now when I smell sulfur? Why does the dude at the checkout counter have to scream at me to break my stare at the CONVEYER BELT? Why is there so much coal?
You wanna know why?
Factorio. Click buy.

This game, especially for a free to play, really impressed me, it succesfully combined features of arcade zombie games ( horde-survival modes, objective modes, different zombie types ... ) with extremly realistic dynamics ( such as bleeding, getting infected, having to manage your inventory and your stamina ) in a mix that can entertain both the casual and the hardcore zombie survival player.
However, the game is not without flaws, Il'l put a list of what I think is good and what I think it's bad about this game:
Good:
-Extremly well done official levels, especially for a free to play.
-Good realism concepts, having to take care of your health ( you can get infected and turn! ), your stamina, your inventory.
-Different difficulties make you able to switch from casual-mode to hardcore-survival however you like.
-A lot of mods for this game, especially new maps.
-Good first-person animations, there's an animation for practically every action you do ( healing yourself, reloading, checking how much ammo you have ).
-Decent graphics.
-Fun to play for the first times.
-The same levels can contain different weapons, different objectives and different zombie spawns, making each game-session in the same level feel a bit different.
Bad:
-Few official levels, half of wich being '' survival-mode '', wich feels the same every time.
-Bad third-person animations, often you can't understand what your teammate is doing with the object in his hands.
-Hitboxes and ragdoll collisions could use some improvements, it's really frustrating to get hit from something that shouldn't have hit you in a game where 1 hit can infect you and basically doom you to death.
-Maybe it's just me, however we just couldn't get the private servers up and running, forcing us to join public ones ( often modded with infinite ammo or full of people that wasted items and such ).
-Gameplay is somewhat methodical and repetitive, after the first hours, it kinda got boring for me.
Overall, for a free to play, this is a game I 100% recommend to try out, especially if you don't mind some of the flaws I found ( or if it was just me seeing them! ).

Transistor is beautiful. Almost everything about this game screams quality. The gameplay is fun and unique, or at the very least different from any other game I've ever played, with a turn-based power that's still completely action beat-em-up, that oddly enough reminds me of the slow-motion from The Matrix movies. The visuals and sound are phenomenal. The art of the game is hard to put in words. Cool colors in a night time atmosphere with sparkling lights. The game is just pretty. The music fits every scene and fight, and makes it that much better. The story is both detailed, complex, and a bit vague. Why everything happened before the start of the game wasn't entirely clear to me when I played it. However, the two main characters' story and their relationship is great enough that it's easy to get attached. You want everything to be okay. You get immersed in their world. The only truly negative think one could say about this game is that it's short, with little replay value. But for the time that it lasts, it is one hell of a ride. I like to think I'll come back and relive it again one day. If you were a fan of Bastion, don't hesitate. Buy this game. And the soundtrack too. It's worth every penny.

When I heard that the developer behind Bastion was releasing another game, I assumed it would be steeped in music, beautiful and stunning visuals, and an enigmatic, emotional story. I was right on all counts. The only drawback is that it's hard not to make comparisons to Supergiant's first game.
The combat mechanics of Transistor are interesting and fun; and thankfully, as the game is not that long, you don't have time to grow tired of them before seeing the end credits. (Of course, the limiters and ability to replay the story means you can ramp up the difficulty as much as you'd like.)
Of course, what I really wanted was the music; the soundtrack of Bastion is worth the price of the game by itself, and while Transistor's music doesn't quite haunt you the way Zia's Theme or Zulf's Theme might, it is evocative and beautiful in its own right. And, like Bastion, the voice acting is once again outstanding.
Interesting game mechanics, fantastic music, stylish and interesting visuals, and a gripping story -- any of these would be reason enough to recommend the game, and Transistor has all of them.

The trading system in this game is tied to paying real money to trade with your friends. Selling things on the marketplace eats up a chunk of the in-game currency as "tax." 30% of it, I think.
The most abominable thing of all, however, I feel, the thing that literally made me write the game off and uninstall it and never want to play it again. Movement speed is universal in the game. Everywhere, no matter what class you are, where you are (in town, safe zone, or battle or boss map), movement speed is universal. If you pay real life money to get a token, you gain 3% movement speed. You may think 3% is not that fast but go ahead and play and really experience it. Imagine if you can move 100 meters an hour. But someone else can move 103 meters an hour. The ENTIRE GAME is moving from place to place. If you are 3% slower than someone else, they are able to complete objectives, get from place to place, so much faster than you can. See an enemy on the map? They'll always beat you to it. Per unit of time they will grind more enemies than you, get more drops than you, move further than you, complete more quests than you. Movement speed advantage is compounded literally every second of gameplay.
The problems with this game just goes on and on. I don't care if this is free to play. Maplestory is a more enjoyable grind. Just about any other game out there is a more enjoyable time sink. Skip Tree of Savior unless they change the gameplay drastically this game is simply not worth it.

I have put an unfortunate amount of hours into this game for a few reasons-
1.It's game play is my favorite out of any moba I've played to date.
2.I am also a mythology buff so the aesthetics of the game really appeal to me.
3.And I also have a few friends that play this quite often and so it's something we can play together.
Now the 3 reasons were for a long time all I needed to keep playing, however this game has a plethora of balancing issues that have plagued the game since I started playing it. From gods to items to certain team comps you can almost always be assured that if you play these gods and get these items then you can win against players with much more experience with minimal effort. So one major counter argument you can make against this complaint "well then why don't you play those gods with those items". To which I would respond with, frankly those gods are boring as all hell to play. They take minimal skill to use, hence why most of these gods usually fall into the "easy" difficulty rating, However despite their ease of use they generally do ridiculous damage or harder to kill than the mythical beings they are based off of. Also this game has a few different game modes that you can play so as to provide some variety to people who don't want to only play conquest(the quintessential game mode of all moba games, with a 5 member team on a 3 lane map). The other major game modes are joust(a 3v3 1 lane game mode for smaller parties) and arena(a 5v5 no lane match where the objective is to whittle down the other teams points by killing enemy gods, or minions, and/or escorting your minions to the enemy base). Now I really like that it has these other game modes however gods are only balanced for conquest making certain gods(especially tanks) in other game modes incredibly broken,making the other game modes much harder to enjoy. Now I have had a lot of fun playing this game but I frankly don't feel like it's worth the time or monetary investment have been worth it in the end. On a final note I still think this game has a lot of potential to be great, but Hi-Rez needs to refocus on balancing and improving the game that they do have instead of piling on more gods and content to make the game seem more appealing with the bloated numbers of gods and game modes

First of all, I must say I was quite unhappy when this game came out. On the other hand, I'm writing this review because I strongly disagree with a lot of what is said in the reviews. I'm a huge fan of Total war series. I played a lot on my old computer and this account doesn't reflect the amount of time I've put in this series. I easily played thousands of hours of this series. A lot of the earlier game were bought outside of Steam. Rome 1 was my favorite by far. I anticipated this game for so long, it was ridiculous. Probably the game I was the most eager to play in my life (after Final Fantasy 7.. obviously..). But then it came out. Everthing in this game was less than I expected. The overall control of your faction (science, culture,etc.), the gameplay in battle, the variety of unit and building, everything was off for me. I expected the game to give you more control over your faction and how you wish to direct it. It was quite the opposite. So I stopped playing it after about 30 hours of gameplay feeling I got robbed by CA.
Then emperor edition came out. It was better in a lot of ways, but still not enough for me. I stopped playing.
Then, I saw their was a lot that was being done in the workshop, so I tried a few of those mods. This is when I got hooked. Mixing different mods in a strategy game like this is what made this game the best of the Total war series for me. (even if is not exclusively because of CA, they made the workshop mods available in the first place) This is when I got the control I've always wanted over the parameters of my campaigns. The community achieved what everyone expected in the first place.
Could this game be better? Obviously, and in a lot of ways. Is this a good game? Hell yeah. The problem all started at the start of this review : the expectation. People had Total War in such a great esteem that they expected the sequel of the best game of the series to be a masterpiece, nothing less. And as in every franchise, your success is also your downfall. People can't accept anything but improvement. If you launch a sequel that is not better, but different, people will spit on it : ''How come you had that much time and didn't put everything I had in mind'' they say, ''If I could think of it, how could you not?''
I think CA failed big time with this game launch, and even with the improvement and DLCs. That said, I believe this is worth 60 dollars anytime. If you don't believe me, even the people that doesn't recommend this game spent at least 200 hours+  on it... Quite ironic I'd say, when you consider a lot of people will not hesitate to spend 10 dollars to play a game for 20 hours. BTW, if you're buying it, I recommend you try the Divide et Impera mod. It is better than the original game. This is not, however the funniest of mods mix. Try them out and I assure you'll have hours of fun ;)

When I heard that the developer behind Bastion was releasing another game, I assumed it would be steeped in music, beautiful and stunning visuals, and an enigmatic, emotional story. I was right on all counts. The only drawback is that it's hard not to make comparisons to Supergiant's first game.
The combat mechanics of Transistor are interesting and fun; and thankfully, as the game is not that long, you don't have time to grow tired of them before seeing the end credits. (Of course, the limiters and ability to replay the story means you can ramp up the difficulty as much as you'd like.)
Of course, what I really wanted was the music; the soundtrack of Bastion is worth the price of the game by itself, and while Transistor's music doesn't quite haunt you the way Zia's Theme or Zulf's Theme might, it is evocative and beautiful in its own right. And, like Bastion, the voice acting is once again outstanding.
Interesting game mechanics, fantastic music, stylish and interesting visuals, and a gripping story -- any of these would be reason enough to recommend the game, and Transistor has all of them.

Bastion, being one of my favorite titles, created high expectations for Supergiant Game's second title, Transistor. The trailers and previews promised two things that we've already come to expect from Supergiant Games: Fun, decisive combat, and a great soundtrack.
First and foremost, Transistor is a great game, and it's definitely worth a buy, especially if you have already played Bastion and enjoyed it too. I just feel like Transistor was just short of perfect and it bothered me. The combat is great and the Function system is new and refreshing and makes for a crazy ammount of choices to make. The gameplay offers way more strategy than was present in Bastion, and for that it's great.
My problems with Transistor lie in the Beach safehouse areas you encounter throughout the game. They offer these kind of tutorial/challenge modes and I feel like I was encouraged to complete them all because I didn't understand what were the real benefits to doing so. You find out that doing these challenges unlocks extra music to listen to in said safehouse- but that's where the problem is. You have this great soundtrack, great motivation to advance the story and yet both of those are wasted in this boring challenge area. The soundtrack, while great in it's own right, does not have an impact to the story as much as it should because half of it is locked away in this area. Heck, doing these challenge courses took up nearly half of the playthrough. The music should have been rewarded to players by playing through the story, not by doing these intermission challenges.
That is my only gripe with it though. Transistor shows that Supergiant Games is more than able to keep making top-down isometric strategic-action games and keep it refreshing, yet comfortably similar. Darren Korb rocking the music is always a huge bonus.
I can't decide, it's either a solid 8 or 9/10.

Transistor, to me, is beautiful. If someone doubts that video games can be an art form, show them this game.
The art style, music, voice acting, and somewhat open-to-interpratation story make what would be a short, fun sci-fi RPG into an incredible experience, through and through. The gameplay has a surprising amount of depth as well, since you can use any given "Function" as an active ability, an upgrade to another ability, or a passive ability. It's satisfying to mix and match functions to create new abilities. What's more, the semi-turn-based gameplay works really well. You can fight in real time, then plan out a precise and devastating series of moves. And even though it's short, there are lots of ways to keep the game fresh, to extend your play time far past the first playthrough. In addition to a New Game+ playthrough, there are numerous challenges and "limiters" you can use to customize your difficulty, reminiscent of Halo's "skulls".

Where to begin with this game.  Well, let's go over the basics.  It's a survival/craft game that can end up being rather nasty to you, mostly by other players.  The best way I could describe this game is that it's a Medieval version of Rust, but, let's actually dig into a proper review here.
Graphically, the game is mixed in my honest opinion.  The environment can be outright beautiful, though most of the models are...  Kinda meh, which may be due to the character creator giving you sliders to mess with, making it so you could either look like a gnome or a troll.  Animations could be better, but, that's what you get for a unity engine game.
Mechanically, construction is block based on a static map, which at the time of writing this review, there's only 2 maps, which both are unique and offer their own play-style.  There's land claims, which this game is essentially built around a focus of PVP rather than PVE (Fighting for the throne and the construction of siege weaponry).  The physics are kinda awkward and at times, outright deadly.  Quick example, based off a personal experience.  Climbed up a mountain to get a good view of the surrounding land.  Slipped off one edge, and started rapidly sliding down hill, and kinda just stopped in the middle of a field after dodging rocks and trees on my trip down.  Got the worst idea of "I'm going to do that again, that was fun!"  and ended up wrapping myself around a tree, essentially instantly killing myself.
It's worth a look at whenever it goes on sale, or if you're one of the more hardcore types of players that absolutely loves PVP along with the survival/crafting game archetype, then this would be for you.

Being a long time Elder Scrolls fun, I could not wait to get lost in Tamriel. However the game straight after it got published was rather boring, the map felt like a grinding pit, so after a month I put the game away for a while, than Morrowind came, and I felt it's time for another try and oh boy. The quests are amazing, it really feels like this is an RPG with Multiplayer elements and this is what really made ESO fun. It doesn't force you to play with people if you don't want to, altough the dungeons, the trials, the pvp is also unique and fun but never played an MMO before which I played for the quests too, and that's where this game really gets me, funny or sometimes sad dramatic stories really helps me to get lost in the huge map. Never come across with a quest where I had to simply kill 10 of something or collect 20 of else, instead I had to help rebuild a kingdom, help to pull a prank on a mage who is allergic to cats, get drunk a couple times, and help a nord to merry an orc.
The war for Cyrodil never stops, and the new battlegrounds are good fun too. Dungeons and Trials are not the strongest part of the game still they all fun and they never felt too boring or repetitive.
In conclusion, this is the best MMORPG at the moment on the market, with easy 600+ hours of fun in it, even more thankfully the regualry coming DLCs.
Buy it if you are in search for an MMORPG where you want to invest time in, if you love Elder Scrolls and it's story telling, but if you looking for the Elder Scrolls 6 in this game probably you will be dissapointed for the first couple hours, take my advice join a guild, and explorle Tamriel.

multiplayer:

- worse level design: a lot of corridor like levels exist and a lot of areas would actually collide with each other, plus a giant  castle filled with lava is somehow flying over a windmill....

This game series is notorious for being difficult. However this is a slightly deceiving description. The game isn’t hard. It is very straight forward with a clear path at most points. The reason it is “hard” is because the game forces you to die all the time. Combat revolves around you blocking or dodging an opponent’s attacks. This simply is not possible (due to preparation time of blocking or dodging) unless you have seen the animation before. The only way to see the animation is to have fought and died to the mob before. This essentially means that unless you are incredibly lucky, you will die on every new mob in the game before you can figure out all of its animations, so you know when to block/dodge and attack. To top it off, you lose all of your money/experience every time you die in addition to permanently losing max health. Why this game punishes you for something that it makes you do is beyond me. My recommendation is to save your money and skip this game.

Borderlands 2 was also developed by Gearbox Software and published by 2K Games and was released on September 18, 2012. Like the first installment, Borderlands 2 is a "shoot and loot" game with a series of central quests and numerous side quests. Once again you must choose one of four (or six if you download the two additional characters) vault hunters and take them to a new vault.
However you are not the only one looking for it, Handsome Jack is venturing for it as well and he is a piece of work. Handsome Jack is, in my opinion, one of the best video game villains ever created.
The first character you can choose to be is Axton the Commando. Much like Roland in the first game, Axton's Action Skill deploys an automated Sabre Turret that fires on any enemies within its range. After a few upgrades he is allowed to deploy two turrets at once and can even stick them to walls and ceilings.
The second vault hunter is Maya the Siren. This is the character I chose for my first play through because of her healing abilities. She is also beneficial for herelemental effects and crowd control. Her action skill is Phaselock, which will suspend and immobilize enemies.
The next vault hunter is a short little Mexican named Salvador the Gunzerker. Salvador resembles Brick from the first game as far as abilities are concerned, but instead of powerful melee attacks Salvador's action skill allows him to dual wield any two firearms. Upgrading his skill can allow him to throw multiple grenades at once, regenerate massive ammounts of ammunition and health, or attract enemies with a double middle-finger taunt.
The last vault hunter is a Zero the Assassin whose origins, species and gender are completely unknown. Zero's skills are based on sniping and using a sword for melee attacks. His action skill creates a decoy and turns Zero invisible so he can sneak past or attack enemies.
That completes the list of playable chatacters that are included with the game. The next two can be downlaoded as add on content. The first downloadable character (and my favorite) is Gaige the Mechromancer. Mechromancer? What's that? Well Gaige's action skill is to summon a hulking, floating machine called "Deathtrap" to attack her enemies.
The other downloadable character is Krieg the Psycho. His action skill allows him to go on a rampage using his Buzz Axe to deal highly increased melee damage and refilling his health entirely every time he kills.
The story begins with the vault hunters answering a call from Handsome Jack to find the vault. Unfortunately it's a trap and Handsome Jack attempts to kill all the vault hunters by blowing up the train they are riding.
From that point on he constantly tries to take you out, and in turn the vault hunters try to take him out. You aren't alone though, the original vault hunters from the first game help you out periodically throughout the game. And there are a couple of twists involving certain deaths that really keep you on your toes.
Handsome Jack is a very twisted individual, but damn he is funny. This game is definately good for many laughs. Naturally Handsome Jack gets to the vault first and opens it when you arrive unleashing another giant alien creature that you have to kill. Once you kill it you get to kill Jack. In addition to the two extra characters, and countless character skins, there are also four downloadable add on campaigns.
The first one was "Captain Scarlett and Her Pirate's Booty" which, like it sounds, puts you on a treasure hunting quest.
Next was "Mr. Torgues Campaign of Carnage." The objective here was to get sponsored in an arena tournament, and of course enter the arena and leave a champion.
The third add on was "Sir Hammerlocks Big Game Hunt." It is what it sounds like, basically a safari.
And last but definately not least was "Tiny Tina's Assault On Dragon Keep." This one is the best by far. much longer and more content than the rest. I've finished the entire story, and I can certainly say that it's worth every penny, especially if you get it and the OST on sale. I had heard quite a bit about this game, and it definitely met all of my expectations, and even exceeded several. Transistor doesn't hold your hand for very long, nor does it spoonfeed you exposition, but bits and pieces of the story can be decrypted by experimenting with different combinations of functions.
I could gush on and on about how much I enjoyed this game, but it boils down to this...
Audio/Visual:
Flawless. Hands-down the best OST I've heard in recent memory, and the visuals are positively stunning, even on my slightly dated laptop. No fluctuations or hiccups at all.
Gameplay:
Solid, if occasionally gimmicky. If you want to crutch on Turn(), you can, and if you want more of a challenge, play it real-time.
Story:
Present, but assumes you're intelligent enough to connect a few dots. It works well, considering that the protagonist is thrust into a perilous situation with few answers. Just pay attention to cutscenes, because it's not going to be readily repeated if you miss it the first time.
The verdict is as thus: Definitely a game for the artsy type, Transistor is an intriguing journey through the streets of Cloudbank that's worth a look.

This game is a masterpiece. With one of the best soundtracks I have ever heard in a game, with stunning visuals, great voice acting, astounding story, and interesting and unique combat create an experience that must be played.
From the art direction, to the controls, to the Turn() system, this game oozes atmosphere and depth. I love it to bits, and I wish I could play it again and again with the same experience as I did the first time.
My only gripe is that there could have been a few puzzles here and there. This idea was kinda flirted about in the beginning of the game, but never really touched on again. Puzzles would have made this game even more amazing.
Overall, this is a must get. It takes around 8-10 hours to complete, and you will enjoy every minute of it.

In story, Transistor fails in every way its predecessor, Bastion, managed to succeed. Our narrator is less charismatic here than in Bastion. In Bastion you have a storyteller; in Transistor, more of a drunk tourguide. In Bastion the world comes together as you play; in transistor, it is devoid of life. Bastion did so much for a narrative, while giving out very little in concrete detail. In fact, the vagueness of Bastion is a hinge in the storytelling mechanism. For Transistor, the story never really comes together. It seems like the wrong lessons were learned from the successes of Bastion.
Transistor's gameplay, in contrast, manages to innovate a fun style of isometric action, adding a little bit of slow-mo strategy and changing up the weapon modding and levelling enough to make it its own. Oh, and it's pretty too.
Transistor's shortcomings are exacerbated by its maudlin and hopeless tone. It's a fun play-through, but lacks personality and diversity.

The first issue I had with the game was running it. Issues went all over the place with the FPS and the game was nearly crashing even with every setting at minimum or off. I have a computer that could run it just fine, so it's not my PC. Others noted this problem and apparently it's still not fixed, though somehow the game "fixed itself" after I tweaked some things in the game and on my PC, then deleted my profile and restarted. After that, it ran fine with normal/high settings... not sure why, because my final settings were exactly the same as an earlier test that didn't work.
Besides that, the game looks good, sounds good, and plays well (once you figure out the FPS issue, somehow). The story is captivating and in some senses I think the game was more focused on painting a bigger picture with more details than the first game was. The first game had a decent story but it put some weird things together and ended on a somewhat odd note. This game did much better with its lead-up to the finale.
But in terms of environment, it was nowhere near as scary. In some senses, I don't think I would dock the game too much for that. Yes, it's a horror game and it should be scary... but the story was good enough for me to continue playing. I was captivated by that and didn't mind so much that there were less horrifying places (like the prison from the first Amnesia).
In the end, I think that the story of this game is much more memorable than the first game's, but that the first game's environment and areas are more memorable than in this game. Both games have their stronger points, but it would be nice to see a third Amnesia come with a strong story, lots of horror, and terrifying and memorable environments altogether.

Let me start off by saying the game is a lot of fun and addicting. It has a beautiful environment, nice map design, good UI/Menu and crafting, and fun combat, etc.
Okay, so with that said, there is obviously 'mixed' reviews here, which really delayed me from buying the game, but when they recently had a 60% off promotion I jumped on it, and I’m glad I did too, as it is a great game.
There seems to be a lot of hate carried over from StarForge, which I do not know the history of, so I can't speak informed about it.  But, I can speak for Reign of Kings now that I’ve played it for 14+ hours in a very short period of time (at the time of writing this review).  Code Hatch is obviously seeing this game through, as they worked with and listened to community feedback, have had regular patches every ~3-5 weeks, and recently entered Beta 1.
Another thing players are complaining about are servers being riddled with hackers and ruining the game.  You’re always going to have hackers no matter what online game you play, but as long as the developers are doing what they can to thwart the hackers, which I have seen Code Hatch doing via EAC, etc.
Now, when I first started playing the game I did not have a good experience the first couple servers I logged into; one did have hackers, and another I was pretty much KOS’d (Killed On Sight) by a couple of armored-up players.  Well I should say I was COS’d (Captured On Sight)!  I had just logged into this server, was naked with only a driftwood club to defend myself against the two armored players who immediately ganged up on me, captured me, tied a rope around my ankles, dragged me to their base, put me in restraints, and beat me to death.  All in the first 5 to 7 minutes………..
So I’ll conclude my review with some suggestions for a better game experience out the gate:
1)	Servers:  If you like PVP, PVE, or both, then I suggest finding servers with descriptions\info that suit your play style.  From my experience you’re better off finding ‘Community’ servers with regular Admins, which I was lucky to find a few good ones upon my third time playing.  I could be wrong, but I think the ‘Official’ servers are more tainted than the ‘Community’ ones.  Also, find ones that are “NO KOS”.
2)	Review the forums and read information from the developers: Their road map, milestones that have been reached, further plans/implementations, when they expect to go gold, etc., to help you form your own educated opinion and decision.
Anyway, I hope my review helps you make a good decision with no regrets.   :-)

This game is AWESOME.
Bad things first: The engine is chunky. Alt-tabbing crashed the game for me, as did unplugging my controller.
The duels are meh. They control awkwardly and feel very random in their outcome.  The timing doesn't feel consistent, as does dodging bullets. I didn't like them at all. Also why can I take rifle bullets to the chest and walk away but then a single revolver hit to the leg suddenly kills me?
Also the AI is your bog-standard braindead shooting gallery. Meh.
Now to the good stuff:
The gunplay feels really good, and the little extra mechanics in combat aren't bad, either. Focus/bullet time is pretty common these days, but that luck-mechanic where you can dodge an otherwise deadly shot is fricking cool!
Hitting someone with a full blast of buckshot never gets old as well, but what makes it great in this game is the use of sound, the feedback is great.
The music is very fitting to the theme, as is the overall gritty aesthetic of the game and the drawn cutscenes. It just looks good, even if the engine tends to crap out and pop-in objects right before your eyes.
Last but certainly not least: The voice-acting and storytelling are Phenomenal. (Yes, with a capital P).
It's one of the best singleplayer campaigns I ever had in a singleplayer shooter. The way the story is told, retold, sometimes from different standpoints and misconceptions built into the gameplay.... awesome! I want more games that tell stories this good while being fun to play at the same time.

I was pretty excited for this game.  It's an action RPG.  developed by the same guys who developed Bastion.  Nice art style.  So, when it went on sale, I snatched it up right away.
Overall, I was pretty disappointed.  I found the gameplay very repetitive, the action very underwhelming, the story bland and  on the whole very short and unchallenging.  There was a lack of enemy variety, and no real strategy needed to get by them.  Bosses were kind of a pushover too.
Even tho I found this game disappointing, I'll likely give future games from the developer a shot.  Despite my complaints listed above, I enjoyed the actual gameplay mechanics.  The upgrade system was kinda neat and I liked testing out different combinations of attacks you get.  Controls were decently responsive and fluid enough for purpose.  Some other pros are the art style and music.  But, graphics and music don't make a game.  I feel it's more or less wasted here.
To wrap it up.   While the gameplay mechanics, art and music were great.  The repetition, weak challenge, and bland story (no real character development either?) dragged it all down to create a forgettable experience.
One little unrelated complaint too.  The guy trapped in the transistor just never shuts up.  I get it's supposed to be a narrative.   But, holy hell..  a line between narrative and constant irritating rambling blurred together here.

Overall it's a great game - just make sure you know what you're getting.

Modern Warfare 2 is, in my opinion, by far the best Call of Duty game to date. Its Single player campaign will last you anywhere from 6-12 hours depending on the difficulty and if you decide to collect all the intel. The story starts 5 years after the first Modern Warfare and I thought it had a great ending. If it was the last Modern Warfare game without the cliffhanger ending it would be almost perfect. the Spec Ops mode is a Co-Op oriented multiplayer mode that puts you and a friend together to take on a few mini missions. These are extemely fun and can be played solo, but I HIGHLY recommend you get a friend. Overall Spec-Ops is a great addition to the game and I enjoy it more than zombies. I dont really play the multiplayer so I cant give my thoughts on it, especially since its mostly high ranked players and hacked lobbies full of modders. I Highly recommend you get Modern Warfare 1 and 2 if youre looking for some good First Person Shooters with a decent story and amazing set pieces.

If you are after a review of the Singplayer or Special Ops then my review will not help you. It will focus purley on the Multiplayer... I mean isn't that what 'most' of us play Call of Duty for?
Lets start with the map design... There is much variety between each of the maps. They range from Small, Medium and larger sized maps. Rust being the smallest, and Wasteland being the biggest. They sute each play style. Take ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ for example. You can run and gun through the corridors with an SMG or Shotgun, run around the outside of the map with an Assault rifle, or camp at either of the team spawn points with a Sniper rifle.
The weapons are reasonibly well balanced, but there a few that are overpowered, and those are the weapons EVERYBODY uses... ACR, Scar-H, AK-47, UMP45, Intervention and the Spaz 12 are the most common you'll see being used. Then there are Noob Tubes, and Riot Shields. DO NOT get me started on those!
The killstreaks are fun to use, and are lethal, but earning a Tactical Nuke is far too easy to earn. Get a 7 killstreak, call in a Harrier strike, and you'll reach 25 in no time, as long as you stay a live.
The perks are balanced well enough, except for Stopping Power, which increases weapon damage. As if the weapons weren't over powered enough! And One man army, which in theory is a great perk. But it doesn't work well in practice.
The attatchments and camo's take a while too earn, and you'll have to grind through challenges to do so, but you earn a ton of Experience Points (XP) in the process.
The levelling system is, too me, near perfect. You'll reach 30 in no time, but then it starts to become a climb... Once you reach 70, you can of course Prestige and do it all again.
There is also a decent variety of game modes. Team Dethamtch, Free for All, Capture the Flag, Domination, Search and Destroy, Demolition... And my favorite Team Tactical. A mix between mods, 4v4.
Modern Warfare 2 is a must buy for any Call of Duty fan. The community is still pretty active, but it is sad to say there are a lot of hackers, which ruin the experience.

This game is AWESOME.
Bad things first: The engine is chunky. Alt-tabbing crashed the game for me, as did unplugging my controller.
The duels are meh. They control awkwardly and feel very random in their outcome.  The timing doesn't feel consistent, as does dodging bullets. I didn't like them at all. Also why can I take rifle bullets to the chest and walk away but then a single revolver hit to the leg suddenly kills me?
Also the AI is your bog-standard braindead shooting gallery. Meh.
Now to the good stuff:
The gunplay feels really good, and the little extra mechanics in combat aren't bad, either. Focus/bullet time is pretty common these days, but that luck-mechanic where you can dodge an otherwise deadly shot is fricking cool!
Hitting someone with a full blast of buckshot never gets old as well, but what makes it great in this game is the use of sound, the feedback is great.
The music is very fitting to the theme, as is the overall gritty aesthetic of the game and the drawn cutscenes. It just looks good, even if the engine tends to crap out and pop-in objects right before your eyes.
Last but certainly not least: The voice-acting and storytelling are Phenomenal. (Yes, with a capital P).
It's one of the best singleplayer campaigns I ever had in a singleplayer shooter. The way the story is told, retold, sometimes from different standpoints and misconceptions built into the gameplay.... awesome! I want more games that tell stories this good while being fun to play at the same time.

With 184/6  2 Cleric/Kravis/Sadhu, recently quitted the game because of these reasons.
1.Monster bottleneck - There are many maps that monster spawned less than people who is farming there. It causes many people start suffering to farm on the items they need. Especially on a quest items that the npc required.
2.Quest bottleneck - At a later time (mostly when you are about to change class. For example, around level 70s, 170s) you will find out that there is no quests that match out your level and you have to do a quest that mostly overleveled of your characters. Some maps are +10 of your level and the monster of that area usually more than 10 level of your characters and the game make a penalty to increase the mobs damage more than usual.
3.EXP card system - The card system makes the group of players scattered apart. Many people start "not to use" there exp cards and grind out like a guide founded in Reddit. It causes some of the players to left behind since there is a quest bottleneck. People who spent out all there cards will have a hard time to find party to match out their level in both maps and instance dungeons.
4.Lagness, delay and instability - It has been improved somehow since the first day of the server, but there are still some bots, bugs and spammers around the server.
5.Limited in trading - This one is a mandatory system that should be implemented for the players to trade freely. It should not be blocked and give this advantage to the player who is willing to pay for a real money. The reason "to block an RMT player out" or "controlling the game economy" is not quite strong enough since the economically design allowed the people to trade out the "cash items" between the players. It shows that the company is indirectly supported the RMT.
6.Limited amount in instance dungeon/mission joining - For the same reason of #5, they are trying to control the players out not to receive more experience and items. Basically to slow down the players progress and cause the boredom of the game to people since there is nothing to do. It is related to #1 and #2 I have mentioned above since you are hitting the huge wall  between job changes or starting on an end game phrase.
7.Flooding of RMT/scammer in town - You can see this on a main starting towns. Bots keep spamming the message and create the lagness/annoying to the players since they are located at a major point such as a warping fountain, repairman or shops.
8.Monster spawning time in some maps and oddly drop rate - From #1, we can see that not only there are less monster on some area, monster spawning time are also awfully adjusted. Some of them are up to few minutes to be respawned and cause people to keep waiting for it forever. Also, some monsters are even harder to get the items since it has really low drop rate such as a red Infrorocktor who drops a Red infrorocktor shells at Mage Tower 3F. It is insanely takes around one full day to get just 2 pieces to turn them into an npc. (based on my and my brother experience who is done the quest at a different time because the quest is spawned from daily npc in Fedimian).
9. Monster stats are not evenly balanced - Some monsters have an insane amount of hp that have to use "full combo" to get rid just one monster down while many other monsters in the same map use only few hits of the skills to take them down. The hp of that insane mobs are 10 times larger than the other mobs in the same map.
10.Game doesn't suited for solo player - I understand that "game online" is based on the multiplayer that has to group up together to achieve some hard quests. However, this game is so hard even just trying to do some  basic quests. Mostly when you are entering the stage before the ending game (around 170s) you will find out that there will be actually no suited quests available for you. Many classes have to give up due to the lack of something such as dps, sustainable and few players to party with since many of the high players are premade group who is aiming for group battle. Also, the matchmaking system for instance dungeon are really bad.
11.Class (un)balance - Most of the class you will see in the server today are the archer/mage based class that can boost out a maximum possible damage, wave clear. And the class that mostly rare to find is support based. The more level you have, less cleric-base support class you can find in the instance dungeon because this based class is really hard to grind up. (Even my character has to play as a attack/support to keep up the level when soloing since it is really hard to find the party to leech the experience). It creates a lag of class variety since the game has a strong point of many various class you can choose, but there are few classes that really effective (OP) and make the people only play few of the classes.
12.Limited number of people to join queue when it reaches the maximum number that server can handle - Not only on  a character login state, but on the instance dungeon. This limited number has been lately fixed.
13.Some of the quests are carelessly created without an actual test - Some of quest are hardly to do such as a monster dragged quest that has to lure the monster near to the location and killed. Since there is #1, monster usually spawned really less and has to wait for a really long time. You have to spend up to few hours to done the quests. You cannot pulled out the mobs further away from the quest point because the faraway mobs will reset the threat and relocate back to the initial position. Also some quests like "Carving the pillar" has absurdly long delayed time that the npc will spawn to get the quest. This quest has to wait around 2 hours for npc to spawn up for 5 minutes to done that quests.
14.Do not have a global quest tracker - You will never know that you are missing some quests unless you are using an add-on (that is legally to use in game) and causes many players underleveled they should be. (For add-on information, search "Tree of savior add-on Manager" and you will see many useful add-on that developers "should" implemented them on their server).
15. Randomly froze while loading - Sometimes when you are changing the channel or maps, the loading screen is struck at 75% and you have to close and re-open the client. I'm not sure this one has been fixed or not.
16. Skill cooldown does not relate to skill used and mana - You can see that some class based has unfairly amount of cooldown time. For my experience is cleric magic based class. You have one full wombo-combo skills set and has to wait around 30s to use that combo again. From #9, you can see that it takes loads of time to beat out few mobs. The upgrade system was kinda neat and I liked testing out different combinations of attacks you get.  Controls were decently responsive and fluid enough for purpose.  Some other pros are the art style and music.  But, graphics and music don't make a game.  I feel it's more or less wasted here.
To wrap it up.   While the gameplay mechanics, art and music were great.  The repetition, weak challenge, and bland story (no real character development either?) dragged it all down to create a forgettable experience.
One little unrelated complaint too.  The guy trapped in the transistor just never shuts up.  I get it's supposed to be a narrative.   But, holy hell..  a line between narrative and constant irritating rambling blurred together here.

Sequel to the best game ever made isn't as great as it's predecessor. Dark Souls 2 feels like fan made game when compared to the first game. Everything feels lacking: level design, monster/boss design and the lore of the game. PvP is more enjoyable for me though. Despite the games problems it's still a very good game and a must buy for any souls fan.

First off, let me say I'm a huge Souls fan. Demon Souls was a refreshing game, and Dark Souls  really polished off that formula.
Dark Souls II, however, rode the coattails of it's ancestors. Don't get me wrong, it's fun, challenging, and beautiful in almost every way... but it doesn't add anything new. This game tries to further improve upon the formula... but it wasn't made by the same team. This game seems to be a reimagining of the series, but fails in numerous areas. Boss battles, PvP, and gameplay seem just... off. I don't know if it was them trying to be... next-gen, but it just seems off. It's hard to put into words. Things feel very cheap (some areas are just stupidly hard for no real reason. It's like, "I Wanna Be The Guy" at some points) and (some) boss battles are unoriginal. I get that the game is supposed to come off as challenging, but some of it is just unfair. One should be able to judge an area, CAREFULLY STUDY IT AND PLAN IT OUT, and figure out a course of completion. Instead, you get a room with a BUT WAIT THERE'S MORE kind of feel that it didn't need.
Also, so many little tricks that make boss fights easier are just stupid. It's catering to casual players with that. (Lost Sinner, the poison boss, etc.)
It's a very fun game, however. Just don't go in with the same mindset as the earlier games. Just think of it as... a new test for your "Souls" skills. Also, the REAL game starts at NG+. Good luck... and don't go hollow.

Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs was a game that i really waited because i liked Amnesia: Dark Descent and its nice scary atmosphere and creepy monsters.
First moments in Machine for Pigs were good because of the good scary atmosphere and you didnt know what kind of monsters the game have, and sometimes you got scared by tiny jumpscares wich keeped the atmosphere up. It kind of felt that the game will be like Dark Descent, Unfortunately after you see the monster first time, the scary atmosphere kind of vanishes because the monster itself isnt so scary. Tough the few jumpscares and "ONE" particular monster keeps scaring you, i was really disappointed of the "Horror" part oh this game. If we compare Amnesia: DD and MfP as horror games, it feels like MfP isnt horror game at all. I would more likely categorize it as agonizing game. Few things what makes it lose its Scary feeling is that you have lamb WITHOUT oil meter, Wich means you can use your lamb all the time without worrying that your oil will suddenly end. There is no need to hide in closet, because when you use your light and those "monsters" are getting close to you it starts to go on and off. When you are near monsters it flashes fast so you know that you need to turn your light off and just go littlebit backwards behind some boxes or barrels and wait until it walks past you.
Tough the game itself doesnt seem to be so scary it has amazing story in it. At the beginning of the game you really cant get into it so well but if you keep following it and you listen all the conversations and read all the notes what you find you soon notice how depressing and oppressive it is, and how much the game offers you with its story. The story of this game is only reason why i would recomend this game for people. The horror part of this game seems to be so small that i would more likely keep it as nice extra for this story what you play. In my opinion Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs is more one depressing and oppressive but still amazing story, wich have few puzzles and some jumpscares and horror scenes in it.

a major step-down as a sequel to one of the most anticipated Horror Games of it's time. It requires too much rendering for it's average graphics, the whole thing plays like a train (meaning that it's linear), the scares are all scripted jump scares, and it takes no less than 3 hours to complete... also everything that was scary and fun about the Dark Descent is not in this one- there's no collecting notes, no solving puzzles- reducing it's play factor, exploration is a no choice, and everything, every object is tact down- which meant no Stephanos or Tiny Box Tims (and for those who get those references, I can say this game made me miss those)
I also must mention how it's storyline plays out like a waterdowned Bioshock, plot twist and all. And the only thing this game has to relate to the first game is that it lazily throws in references from the Dark Descent; and it all feels so cheap
So without real gameplay, without the genuine thrill of being scared, all for the sake of making a cheap interactive horror movie that can't really play. And even with the arguement that this is better than most other horrors, I never play a horror game that I know is going to fail; because why spend money on something you know doesn't deliver.
Honestly, I have had Minecraft gameplay that's scared me more than this whole game
Fans of Horror, avoid this one and just buy the first one (it also has mods and a well made mini-horror)!!

Call of Juarez Gunslinger may not be the best shooter game on steam,
but it may very well be the best western game you will find on steam.
Story: the story centers around Silas Greeves who sits in a bar telling everybody
about his life as a bounty hunter, and the events that lead him to where he is now.
the story is told in a very special way, since the game tells you the story while you walk through the world.
this is kind of hard to explain, but all you need to know is that it's told in a way no game has done ever before
(so far i know)
Graphics and environment: The graphics would be best described as walking through a painting.
all the environments look like they are taken from some painting or history book.
The environments are also really diverse. in the beginning of the game you start of in a town, but along your journey you will find many different places like,mines,woods,canyon's, and so on.
Gameplay: This part consists of 2 parts. Shootouts, and Duals.
when you play a level you fight yourself through the hordes of bad guys and then you get to a dual.
Shootouts: this consists of you working yourself a way through the level, with your arsenal of guns.
this arsenal consists of shotguns,rifles,dynamyte, and ofcourse revolvers.
there is is also a bar that fills up when you make kills, this is used to activate the slowmotion ability.
this ability is very helpful, probably even necessary on hard difficulty.
the gameplay is very fun and addictive, but may be repetitve for some people.
Duals: this part consists of a showdown between you and another cowboy/legend.
most of these duals put you up against very special people known from old story's and movies.
examples are: Johnny ringo, The sundance kid, butch cassidy, and a lot more.

So, if your looking at this review, you've likely seen the bad rep that this game has gotten over its what, close to four year lifespan? I won't lie to you, on release this game was easily the third biggest turd to have graced this excellent series in its decades long life span. However, that was then, this is now and with all due honesty, after three and a bit years worth of patching and some community modding (I reccomend Radious, as with all Total war games) this game is finally what it really should have been all those years ago. Featuring an extensive campaign map stretching from the British Isles down to Northern African all the way across to the lands of the disstant east, Rome Two is one of the most ambitous Total war games to date (which is probably why it failed so hard initialy) and at this point in time carries it off quite well. True, the AI can occasionally derp, the diplomacy system seems practically rigged against you and sometimes you cant help but feel like there are far more factions that hate you than you deserve. I hate all this but at this point of writing, I have over 170 hours in game because when this game is good it is balls to the wall absoloutley ♥♥♥♥ing AMAZING! I kid you not, despite its numerous flaws Rome Two at this point is one of the best Total War games ever developed. Its well balanced, cinematic, it has a smooth as butter UI and on top of all of that no other Total War game manages large scale battles while looking this good and not running like a fat kid with asthma. (with the exception of warhammer, but thats another review entirely) I love this series and I love this game and you will too, you just need the patience to get to the good bits. Have fun.

Empire was a step in the right direction, conducted in a terrible fashion. Napoleon attempted to pick up the pieces, but napoleon was too small a scope to do it alone. Shogun was alright, but ultimately did not grab most fans enough to define the series. Then came rome 2.........dear god, rome 2, you were the chosen one. Every total war fan highly anticipated your arrival. You were the most hyped total war in history. All fans, old, and new awaited your release..........and then it released, and instantly people experienced probably the worst total war game launch in history. This game is no doubt the primarily killer of the old total war fanbase. This game, is what truly signaled, that the dark age of the total war franchise had begun. From the broken mechanics, to the even more broken gameplay. Almost everything about rome 2 is worse then its predecessors. The AI has always been a very glaring problem in the franchise, but here, in this game, the AI seems to be at its absolute worst of any total war. Even the graphics are a downgrade from the lush, and rich graphics that shogun 2 and napoelon were capable of. How do you manage to make a game, that is worse then its predecessors in almost every way, is beyond me, but rome 2 did it. There are a few things rome 2 did actually do better then previous total wars however. Like for instance, I think the campaign is slightly better done, but I think that can be attributed to the fact that the campaign maps cover far more interesting areas then what previous games leading up to rome 2 did. All and all, I'd recommend, if you did not buy this game at launch and thus, become stuck with it in your library like so many did, dont buy this game. You'd probably be better off with Attilla, I think its even cheaper them rome 2.

It's difficult to find a way to recommend this game enough - between the interesting and ambiguous story, the beautiful scenery and art, and the fun and modularly difficult combat, Transistor is a must play.
The game goes to great lengths to tell you just enough up front to keep you moving through the game, and all the holes it leaves can be filled in with careful observation, dilligently seeking it out, and keeping your imagination running - something that the game encourages.
The combat will seem confusing at first, and it will take a while to find your footing. Once you do, everything flows very well, and is a lot of fun. The modular difficulty allows you to ramp things up to challenge yourself, or keep things turned down to keep things less intense and stressful.
And then there's the art and music - both work in tandem to help enhance and deliver the narrative.
Overall, the more you invest yourself into this game, the more you find things to invest yourself in.

Had to stop playing after I realized the only part of the game I liked was the crafting. You can find materials in the world or by breaking down certain types of items like weapons and armor. There are several different avenues (cloth amor, blacksmith, alchemy, woodworking, enchantment and provisioning [cooking]), and the leveling system in ESO is quicker to reward you for progress than Skyrim. Some cities will also "certify" you, meaning you can take the tutorial in any/all the crafting types and then take daily missions to fill quotas, and you get rewarded with xp and bonus materials so it doesn't feel as much like grinding. There are also special research options for weapons and armore to add gems that give special properties. I hope TES6 takes a page from this system.
That said, the rest of the game is just... boring. Like, really ♥♥♥♥ing boring. It's open-world, but the quests all play out the same way: talk to this dude, go find/kill this thing, meet up with some other guy, kill/find the last thing, get reward. The rewards are usually only good to break down into components for crafting because even early on you can make gear better than what you can loot. Maybe that changes in the end-game stages, but I don't see myself ever playing that long.
You can't choose to be good or evil, there are no real branching paths that the quests take, dialog is pretty much limited to 'yes', 'no', and 'what is this?' options, and you can see the plot twists coming a mile away. It feel more like I've been given a laundry list of chores than going out adventuring.
I'll summarize one of the last quests I did: "Go get me these reagents from my dead ancestors so we can summon an ancient daedra to smite these invaders. I'd already tried and they said no, but I'm sure they were just being♥♥♥♥♥♥♥" ... "Hahaha! Look how well my plan worked! Suck it ancestors, I'm amazing!" ... "Oh no! The daedra is too powerful to banish! Why didn't my ancestors warn me??"
I don't play pvp so I can't comment on it, but there isn't much about this game that makes it stand out from any other MMO on the market, so I'd be surprised if the pvp was any different. I want to be clear though: I't not a bad game. The pve game mechanincs are solid, graphics are good, has the standard microtransaction fare that pretty much all MMOs have these days. But the whole time I was playing I kind of just wanted to do something else.
TL;DR: It's got all the trappings of a solid MMO, but it's boring as ♥♥♥♥ because every mission is the same. Great crafting system though.
